# Sirach 12 — Disagreement Log

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** Sirach 12 (18 verses)
**Total Disagreements:** 12

---

## Disagreement 1 — Verse 1

**Issue:** "There will be thanks for your good deeds" — active vs. passive
- EMET: "there will be thanks for your good deeds"
- LOGOS: "your good deeds will find their thanks"
- PNEUMA: "your kindness will actually count for something"
- SOPHIA: "your good deeds will find their thanks"

**Resolution:** PNEUMA's "count for something" is too colloquial and loses the gratitude theme. LOGOS/SOPHIA preferred. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 2 — Verse 4

**Issue:** "Withhold his bread" — how explicit to be about the reason
- EMET: "lest by means of it he overpower you"
- LOGOS: "lest he thereby get power over you"
- PNEUMA: "or they'll use it to gain power over you"
- SOPHIA: "lest he use it to gain power over you"

**Resolution:** Minor variation. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 3 — Verse 5

**Issue:** "Twice as much evil" vs. "double the evil"
- EMET: "twice as much evil"
- LOGOS: "double the evil"
- PNEUMA: "double the harm"
- SOPHIA: "double the evil"

**Resolution:** PNEUMA "harm" softens "evil." LOGOS/SOPHIA "double the evil" more literal. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 4 — Verse 8

**Issue:** Order of the proverb — friend in prosperity, enemy in adversity
- EMET: "A friend is not known in prosperity, nor is an enemy hidden in adversity"
- LOGOS: same
- PNEUMA: "You can't really know a friend until you're both in trouble, and you can't see an enemy's true face until things are going well" — INVERTS the order
- SOPHIA: same as EMET/LOGOS

**Resolution:** PNEUMA inverts and significantly paraphrases. The Greek has friend/prosperity and enemy/adversity in that order. EMET/LOGOS/SOPHIA literal rendering preferred. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 5 — Verse 9

**Issue:** "Even a friend becomes separated from him" — how to render the friend's departure
- EMET: "even his friend becomes separated from him"
- LOGOS: "even a friend goes his own way"
- PNEUMA: "even friends drift away"
- SOPHIA: "even his friend becomes distant"

**Resolution:** All communicate fair-weather friendship. SOPHIA's "becomes distant" slightly softer but natural. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 6 — Verse 10

**Issue:** Bronze corrosion metaphor
- EMET: "like bronze he rusts, so is his wickedness"
- LOGOS: "as bronze corrodes, so does his wickedness"
- PNEUMA: "their malice corrodes like bronze, never going away"
- SOPHIA: "his wickedness corrodes like bronze"

**Resolution:** EMET "rusts" is less accurate for bronze (which tarnishes/corrodes, not rusts). LOGOS/SOPHIA "corrodes" preferred. PNEUMA adds "never going away" as interpretive addition. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 7 — Verse 11

**Issue:** The mirror metaphor — meaning of the image
- EMET: "you will be to him like one who has polished a mirror, and you will know that it did not wholly corrode"
- LOGOS: "treat him like one who polishes a mirror, and know that it will not remain entirely free of rust"
- PNEUMA: "Think of them like a tarnished mirror — no matter how much you polish it, there's always some rust hiding in the metal"
- SOPHIA: "treat him like someone polishing a mirror — know that the rust has not gone entirely away"

**Resolution:** The mirror comparison is complex — the point is that despite apparent improvement (polishing), the underlying corrosion remains. LOGOS/SOPHIA best capture the logical point without over-explaining. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 8 — Verse 12

**Issue:** Consequence of seating enemy at right hand
- EMET: "at the last you understand my words and be stung by them"
- LOGOS: "in the end you will understand my words, and be stung with regret"
- PNEUMA: "In the end you'll understand what I'm saying and kick yourself for not listening sooner"
- SOPHIA: "in the end you will understand my words and be stung by regret"

**Resolution:** PNEUMA too colloquial. LOGOS adds "with regret" as gloss. SOPHIA close to LOGOS. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 9 — Verse 13

**Issue:** "Snake charmer" — level of detail
- EMET/LOGOS/SOPHIA: "snake charmer"
- PNEUMA: no difference in meaning

**Resolution:** All agents agree on "snake charmer." Consistent. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 10 — Verse 15

**Issue:** "He will not stand firm" vs. "he will not hold you up"
- EMET: "he will not stand firm"
- LOGOS: "he will not hold you up"
- PNEUMA: "they won't be there to catch you"
- SOPHIA: "he will not hold you up"

**Resolution:** LOGOS/SOPHIA interpret the Greek as meaning he won't support you when you fall (transitive). EMET's "stand firm" reads as the enemy himself not standing. LOGOS/SOPHIA preferred for clarity. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 11 — Verse 16

**Issue:** "He will not be satisfied with your blood" — bloodthirst image
- EMET: "he will not have enough of your blood"
- LOGOS: "he will not be satisfied with your blood"
- PNEUMA: "he won't stop until he's had your blood"
- SOPHIA: "he will not be satisfied with your blood"

**Resolution:** LOGOS/SOPHIA "satisfied" is more literal to Greek. EMET "have enough" also valid. PNEUMA's "he won't stop" changes the image slightly. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 12 — Verse 17

**Issue:** "Pretending to help" — active deception rendered
- EMET: "pretending to help, he will undermine your foot"
- LOGOS: "while pretending to help, he will trip you up"
- PNEUMA: "acting like they want to help, while tripping your feet out from under you"
- SOPHIA: "while pretending to help, he will trip up your feet"

**Resolution:** PNEUMA's "out from under you" is an elaboration. LOGOS/SOPHIA close. SOPHIA adopted.
